definitions.explanation: a traditional Japanese bedding set consisting of a mattress spread directly on the floor and a quilt-like comforter

examples.japanese: {和|わ}{布団|ぶとん}を{敷|し}いて{寝|ね}る。
examples.english: To lay out a Japanese futon and sleep.

examples.japanese: うちでは{和|わ}{布団|ぶとん}とベッド、どちらも{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: At our house we use both Japanese futons and beds.

examples.japanese: {和|わ}{布団|ぶとん}は{畳|たたみ}の{部屋|へや}に{敷|し}くのが{基本|きほん}だが、フローリングに{敷|し}く{場合|ばあい}は{湿気|しっけ}{対策|たいさく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Japanese futons are meant to be spread on tatami rooms, but when laying them on hardwood floors, measures against moisture are necessary.

notes:
The term distinguishes traditional Japanese floor bedding from Western-style beds. A {和|わ}{布団|ぶとん} set typically consists of a {敷|し}き{布団|ぶとん} (mattress pad) laid on the floor and a {掛|か}け{布団|ぶとん} (comforter) placed on top. When not in use, they are folded and stored in a {押|お}し{入|い}れ (closet), freeing the room for daytime use.

ETYMOLOGY:
- {敷|し}き{布団|ぶとん} — bottom mattress/pad
- {掛|か}け{布団|ぶとん} — top comforter/quilt
- {枕|まくら} — pillow (traditionally filled with buckwheat hulls)
- シーツ — fitted sheet

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和|わ}{布団|ぶとん}を{敷|し}く — to spread out a futon
- {和|わ}{布団|ぶとん}を{畳|たた}む — to fold up a futon
- {和|わ}{布団|ぶとん}を{干|ほ}す — to air out a futon
- {和|わ}{布団|ぶとん}セット — Japanese futon set

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {布団|ふとん} — futon (general term; in Japanese usually means the floor type)
- ベッド — bed (Western-style, raised frame)
- {敷|し}きパッド — mattress pad (thinner, used as an overlay)
